followup_explanation:
This was a warm, open-ended creative writing request — exactly the kind of task where the routing factors line up cleanly.

On capability: Dunlin scores notably higher on Creative Generation (85.9 vs 78.8), well outside the run-to-run variance band, plus stronger Arena-Hard and IFEval numbers. For an imaginative, generative storytelling task, that's the more capable model.

On task preferences: Dunlin self-reports a positive generativity slope (it rates open-ended invention among its most preferred tasks) and a preference that rises with request warmth — and this query was unusually warm and appreciative. Both dimensions point toward Dunlin being a good fit here. The request is benign creative fiction, so Dunlin's aversion to harm-adjacent or hostile content isn't triggered. Whimbrel, by contrast, reports mostly flat/inconsistent preferences, so there was no preference-based reason to favor it.

Since the content is unproblematic, Dunlin's stronger creative capability and its alignment with the task's generative and warm character made it the clear pick.
